fields_unknown.not_material_reason: The brief names no outside system; which receipt reader or mail service to use is a design choice, not a fact of the brief.
Nothing is in users' hands, so there is no load to measure; the open load question that matters is receipts per week (U3).
No peak is named; at a few thousand projected beta users a peak would not change the design.
No speed target is named; suggestions come once an evening, so no latency target would change the design.
A beta with no one on call; the brief's wish to avoid night work is goal G3, and no availability figure would change the first design.
Nothing is stored yet; ordinary backups of one small database cover any plausible answer for a beta.
No one is on call; any plausible answer for a beta leads to the same simple setup.
No one else is named as getting data; any processor chosen later is a design choice.

open_anchors: We have not picked a country to launch in

fields_unknown.not_material_reason: No control is asked for beyond email sign-in; the allergy question (U1) is where security could change.
Nothing is built and no threat is named.

open_anchors: we are not sure what that means legally
fields_unknown.not_material_reason: The legal doubt is about allergies and the launch country, named as U1 and U2; no certification is asked for.

unknowns.question: Will Pantry Pal store users' food allergies?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Allergy data is health data: it raises sensitivity to high and brings stricter rules on consent, storage and security.

unknowns.question: Which country will the beta launch in first?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Germany brings GDPR and Canada PIPEDA; the answer decides the hosting region and the privacy duties.

unknowns.question: How many receipts does a typical user scan per week?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Reading receipts is the main processing load and cost; it sizes the receipt-reading service.

unknowns.question: Which outside services, if any, will the product use?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; any receipt reader or mail service is a later design choice.

unknowns.question: What load is there now?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is in users' hands yet, so there is none to measure.

unknowns.question: When are the busiest moments?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No peak is named; at beta size a peak would not change the design.

unknowns.question: How fast must the app answer?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No speed target is named; suggestions come once an evening.

unknowns.question: What availability does the beta need?
unknowns.why_it_matters: With no one on call at night, the answer would only tune how much managed hosting to pay for.

unknowns.question: How much data may the beta lose?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is stored yet; ordinary backups cover any plausible answer.

unknowns.question: How fast must the beta come back after a failure?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No one is on call; any plausible answer leads to the same simple setup.

unknowns.question: Does anyone else receive users' data?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No one is named; processors are a later design choice.

unknowns.question: Are security controls needed beyond email sign-in?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is asked for; the allergy question is where this would change.

unknowns.question: Are there named threats?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is built and none is named.

unknowns.question: Does any certification or audit apply?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is asked for; the legal doubt is about allergies and the launch country.

assumptions.text: The beta is one region and one small database.
assumptions.why: Two part-time founders, a few thousand projected users and no stated peaks.
